newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends weaker on U.S.-Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends weaker on U.S.-Iraq news.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures fell in active sales near the close of trade on Tuesday as news of the U.S. cruise missile attack on Iraq spurred fresh sales.

"The market brought the Nikkei down on the SIMEX as Osaka had already closed," said one dealer with a Japanese futures house. "We don't think the situation in Iraq is going to develop into a full scale war, but the market was taking the opportunity to sell," he said.
The benchmark September Nikkei contract settled at 20,175 against its previous close at 20,180. A total of some 26,800 lots chanaged hands.
Dealers said the SIMEX Nikkei contract appeared technically oversold, however, and may rebound in the near-term on a technical correction before resuming its downtrend.

"It is oversold now, although the charts show that it is on a technical downtrend. We are expecting a technical rebound to take it up to the 20,350/400 level and see that as a good level to sell," said one technical analyst.

Dealers said that with the benchmark September Nikkei contract having broken technical support at 19,960 and touching a low at 19,930, SIMEX futures may weaken to test support at 19,600 in the days ahead. -- Valerie Lee (65 8703080)
